name: Jeena Sikho Lifecare Ltd
title: Jeena Sikho Lifecare Ltd - 544476 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Ayurveda hospitals and products grew revenue 71% to INR801 crore with 44% EBITDA margin, but Q4 EBITDA was cut by about INR21 crore of one-offs, and management's bed-expansion and 4-5x PAT targets rest on unverified government and insurance rate assumptions.

summary.headline: Jeena Sikho Q4 FY26 revenue rose 55% YoY to INR216 crore, but PAT fell QoQ to INR45 crore after about INR21 crore of one-time charges.
summary.overview: FY26 revenue from operations reached INR801 crore (+71%), EBITDA INR349 crore (44% margin, +1,360 bps) and PAT INR222 crore (+177%), with no debt. Q4 revenue was INR216 crore (+55% YoY) and EBITDA INR78 crore (36% margin), but management attributed the sequential profit drop to about INR21 crore of one-time items linked to labour code, ECL provisioning, Ind AS lease accounting and bonuses. Management said the operating base is stable and pointed to new bed capacity, OTC product launches and insurance/Ayushman scheme tie-ups as drivers. Several answers were unquantified or deflected to a later email follow-up.

financial_highlights.value: About INR21 crore (INR19-20 crore one-time per CFO; ~INR2 crore recurring)
financial_highlights.change: Labour code/ESOP/bonuses ~INR7 crore; ECL ~INR5 crore; leasehold ~INR9 crore; loyalty points ~INR1.25 crore

segments.name: Ayurveda Healthcare Services (hospitals/clinics)
segments.commentary: Private hospital sales rose to INR349 crore from INR136 crore; government sales fell to INR36 crore from INR118 crore. Health insurance share of sales rose to 26% from 4% a year earlier. Services mix about 48% of revenue in the latest period.

segments.name: Ayurveda Healthcare Products (OTC/e-commerce)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR416 crore (52% of total); retail sales rose to INR415 crore from INR215 crore. Q4 medicine sales were INR118 crore vs INR121 crore in Q3. Management said product and services margins are similar, within about 1%.

guidance_outlook: About 2,300 operational beds to reach 2,800-3,000 within 3-4 months; management also said 3,000-3,500 by March 31, 2027.
Target of 7,000-10,000 beds in 3-5 years; revenue target INR3,000 crore in 3-5 years, split roughly 50:50 products and services.
PAT target of 4x-5x over the next 4 years; management said minimum FY27 PAT of INR300 crore.
Expects product sales to show impact from May launches over the next 2-4 months; nine OTC products launched, with more medicines planned for June-July.
Says Ayushman scheme rates of INR8,800-9,400 per day and insurance rates of INR8,800-9,200 per day could lift revenue per bed; the scheme is expected in 1-2 months but is unconfirmed.
capex_capacity: Operational beds about 2,300, with 445 more in active deployment; management said non-operational beds were deliberately held back during the Iran-America conflict due to cost.
Block additions in FY26 were INR42 crore (INR32 crore new assets, ~INR10 crore from WIP).

Planned facilities: large hospital in Lucknow (finalisation this week), Ahmedabad, new property in Patna, Kolkata property found, new Pune centre, Mumbai bed expansion, Panchkula wellness centre in June, ultra-luxury 108-room Manali centre in July.
Claims it can add 2,000 beds within 9-12 months once government payment portal is fixed; seven UP colleges identified.
Setup cost INR3-4 lakh per bed; claims payback under 6 months for small facilities and 71% three-year average ROCE (company claim).
demand_pricing: FY26 IPD volume +65% to 40,450; OPD volume +69% to over 600,000; Q4 OPD/COD/video consult patients +247% YoY, daycare +139%, IPD +84%.

Management attributed a slight Q4 volume dip to deferred preventive bookings in March amid war-related panic; said about 250 advance-booked patients were affected and Meerut census averaged 316 recently.
Repeat rates for last quarter: 26% for admitted hospital patients and 34% for products (products only about 6 months old).
Management computes revenue of INR4,650 per bed-day on 2,300 beds (INR375 crore over 8.28 lakh bed-days), versus average ticket of INR8,000-8,200 per admitted patient.
Government sales were deliberately cut due to delayed payments and credit provisioning; management said private hospital business is the focus.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 OPD, IPD and daycare volumes decline slightly QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed war-related panic in March, when advance-booked preventive patients deferred visits; said only about 250 bookings were affected and volumes have recovered.

qa_highlights.question: Will product sales growth resume after the Entero tie-up, given Q4 medicine sales of INR118 crore vs INR121 crore in Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Entero model stalled because Entero wanted the company to bear costs, so it shifted to newspaper, social media and TV spend and launched two products in May; impact expected in 2-4 months. INR2-4 crore QoQ swings described as immaterial.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR21 crore one-off is recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said INR19-20 crore is one-time (INR7 crore employee benefits and INR5 crore ECL one-time, plus leasehold and depreciation effects) and about INR2 crore is recurring; leasehold impact to be spread evenly from next year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q4 EBITDA margin about 46% excluding one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed with the analyst's framing and cited FY26 EBITDA of INR349 crore on INR801 crore, about 45%, versus INR125 crore (27%) in FY25.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue mix outlook at INR3,000 crore and will margins stay similar?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the mix will be about 50:50 products and services (48% services, 52% products in the latest period) and that both segments will grow in parallel with similar margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the bed addition path to 7,000-10,000 beds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it can add 2,000 beds in 9-12 months once demand and government payment readiness allow; growth may be lumpy and depends on changing public narrative toward preventive care.

risks_watch: Q4 margin is reported after about INR21 crore of items management calls one-time; recurring components (about INR2 crore, plus lease and depreciation changes) need tracking next quarter.
Bed utilisation and volume momentum depend on preventive demand, which slipped in March amid geopolitical headlines; management is betting on 3-4 months to change public perception.
Government business was cut to about INR36 crore from INR118 crore; Ayushman scheme and UP cashless scheme timing is unconfirmed and based on management statements.
Product growth is untested: nine OTC products are under three months old, repeat rates were 34% for products, and several medicine launches were deferred from February.

Auditor transition to Grant Thornton drove accounting changes (advance booking practice, leasehold provisioning, bonuses); the result release was delayed to May 30, 2026, and management did not provide full segment profitability.

Several analyst questions were deflected to a post-call email follow-up; governance and disclosure quality is a watch item, including the earnings call held on June 2, 2026 with the transcript filed June 8.
summary.management_tone: Highly confident and promotional, with bold long-range targets (INR3,000 crore revenue, 7,000-10,000 beds) and frequent references to policy tailwinds. Cautious and deflective on Q4 quarter-on-quarter details, often referring analysts to the CFO or to email follow-ups.
key_quotes: Our company is not a wellness company; it is a mainstream healthcare provider, measured just like any other hospital in India.
I just need to admit 140000 people, and my turnover will reach INR1500 crores.
I am telling you again, all the big hospitals in India, whether Allopathy or Ayurveda, will have to remove their dependency on government business.
I clarify that the Q4 earnings decline is solely due to these one-time items and does not reflect any weakness in the business.

Large hospital in Lucknow (finalisation pending), plus Ahmedabad, Patna, Kolkata, Pune, Mumbai bed expansion, Panchkula wellness centre (June), 108-room Manali
Potential 2,000 beds within 9-12 months, contingent on government payment portal fix; seven UP colleges identified

growth.why: Management guides 2,800-3,000 operational beds within 3-4 months (from ~2,300, with 445 in active deployment) and a 3,000 crore revenue target in 3-5 years, but the brief gives no firm revenue growth % for FY27 and the 2,000-bed expansion depends on an unfixed government payment portal.
